title: Transient-pocket eviction with buddy-repair for KV micro-fractures
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and variable-length sequences produce highly skewed KV allocations on GPUs: short-lived hot tokens create tiny used regions (micro-fractures) between larger live allocations. Over time these micro-fractures increase fragmentation, reducing available contiguous GPU memory for large model state (attention / activation buffers) and forcing over-eviction of long-lived KV entries, which degrades generation quality and raises token cost.

Goal: Implement a lightweight allocator strategy and low-latency background compaction ("buddy-repair") to reduce fragmentation from transient allocations while preserving low tail latency for inference. This ticket defines the allocation policy, compaction triggers, integration points with the continuous batching scheduler, telemetry signals, and rollout plan.
motivation_and_context: We observe a distinct pattern: high QPS workloads with mixed short/long contexts cause the KV arena to develop interleaved small allocations (frequently created and freed each request). The current slab/buddy hybrid leaves small gaps that are expensive to coalesce during critical low-latency paths. Existing compaction runs are heavy and scheduled infrequently, so fragmentation grows between runs. This issue primarily affects Dedicated and Private workloads with constrained GPU headroom and aggressive latency SLOs. Reducing fragmentation yields better packing (lower OOM risk), fewer forced evictions of long-lived prefixes, and improved token-level cost efficiency.
proposal_summary: Introduce a transient-pocket allocation tier and an opportunistic buddy-repair compaction daemon: 1) Allocation: short-lived KV entries (< lifetime threshold) are placed into 'transient pockets' — small pre-bucketed regions that are easier to reclaim without splitting larger slabs. 2) Eviction: pocket eviction is prioritized before moving into slab reclamation; scoring factors consider pocket density and age. 3) Buddy-repair: a background, low-priority process runs during GPU slack windows (scheduler-detected idle/batch gaps) to coalesce adjacent pockets and reconsolidate into larger free spans using a low-overhead buddy-style merge. 4) Scheduler integration: batching scheduler provides micro-idle hints and can request immediate lightweight repairs during inter-batch gaps. 5) Safety: compaction is throttled by time and memory-copy budget; if repair would risk tail latency, it yields.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Alternatives considered: 1) Aggressive inline compaction on free: too disruptive for tail latency. 2) Larger slab sizes to reduce fragmentation: increases internal waste and harms small-request efficiency. 3) Prefetch-style allocation coalescing at request time: requires heavier cross-request coordination and impacts throughput. The chosen approach aims for minimal runtime overhead, bounded compaction costs, and clear separation between hot transient allocations and long-lived KV entries.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (small-gap bytes / total arena) reduced by >= 40% at steady state in mixed short/long synthetic workload
No >5% regression in 99th-percentile per-request latency on staging under production-like load
Compaction background CPU/GPU time budget <= 2% of node utilization during steady-state
Eviction churn for long-lived KV entries reduced by >= 25% compared to baseline
Instrumentation in metrics and dashboards capturing pocket state, repair events, and repair cost
implementation_plan: Draft design doc with allocator state machine and API hooks (this ticket references doc: link below)
Prototype transient pocket allocator in allocator-sim harness; run synthetic churn workloads and measure fragmentation curves
Implement in runtime: allocator tier + pocket bookkeeping + eviction scoring
Add low-priority buddy-repair worker with configurable time/copy budget and scheduler hint interface
Expose feature flag and runtime knobs (pocket size buckets, lifetime threshold, repair budget)
Instrument telemetry: pocket_allocs, pocket_frees, pocket_fragmentation_ratio, repair_runs, repair_time_ms, compaction_failures
Staging rollout: dark traffic (telemetry only) -> canary with 5% traffic -> 25% -> full with rollback guardrails
Post-rollout: run benchmark suite and validate acceptance criteria; update docs and runbook
implementation_notes: Pocket buckets chosen as powers-of-two from 128B to 64KB depending on tokenized KV footprint distribution
Pocket bookkeeping must be lock-free when possible; use per-stream arenas to reduce contention
Background repair should use GPU-to-GPU memmove primitives where available (peer DMA) to avoid CPU round-trips
Maintain mapping invariants to enable quick pointer fixups without large-scale KV rebuilds
Expose a conservative mode for Private deployments with restricted DMA privileges
rollout_and_migration: Feature gated behind runtime flag defaulting to off for existing Dedicated clusters
Start with telemetry-only mode in staging to compare allocator maps without altering runtime behavior
Enable pocket allocation but keep buddy-repair disabled (observe fragmentation improvements)
Enable buddy-repair during off-peak hours and monitor tail-latency closely
If any regression observed, reduce repair budget or revert to telemetry-only mode while hotfix implemented
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: background repair induces tail latency spikes. Mitigation: strict time/copy budgets and scheduler-aware yielding.
Risk: pocket scheme increases internal fragmentation for workloads dominated by large KV objects. Mitigation: auto-detect workload profile and disable pockets when median allocation size > threshold.
Risk: complexity increases debugging cost. Mitigation: comprehensive allocator maps exported to logs and a lightweight map-diff tool for root-cause analysis.
Risk: cross-tenant repair in Dedicated could touch KMS/ACL concerns. Mitigation: repair runs execute within tenant memory domains and respect isolation boundaries.
Risk: DMA is not available on some Private installs. Mitigation: fallback to CPU copy with stricter budgets and disable on unsupported infra
testing_plan: Unit tests for pocket lifecycle and eviction scoring
Allocator simulator fuzz testing with mixed sequence-length distributions
Microbench: measure repair cost and pocket reclaim latency on representative GPU types (A100, H100, and Ampere-equivalents)
End-to-end regression tests in staging job replaying production traffic for 72 hours
Chaos test: inject high-churn short requests while repair runs to validate no SLA violation
